results.title: Understanding Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE) – VWO
results.content: Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE) is a critical concept in any type of testing. By setting a smaller MDE, you can reduce the undetectable range and make your test more sensitive to smaller changes in the conversion rate. * **Balance Sensitivity and Practicality**: While it's tempting to set a very low MDE to detect even minor improvements, this can lead to impractically large sample sizes and extended test durations. Conversely, a larger MDE is preferred for sensitive metrics to detect even minor positive effects. + **Sensitive Metrics (e.g., Time Spent on Page):** These metrics are more prone to change, making it easier to detect positive effects with a larger MDE. + **Optimize test duration:** Adjusting the MDE as the test progresses can help balance the need for detecting smaller effects with the practical constraints of time and resources. MDE helps you strike the right balance between detecting meaningful changes and ensuring your tests are efficient and cost-effective.

results.title: Understanding and Interpreting Effect Sizes in Statistical Analysis
results.content: # Understanding and Interpreting Effect Sizes in Statistical Analysis. Effect sizes are a critical part of interpreting statistical analysis. While statistical significance indicates whether a result is likely due to chance, effect sizes convey the practical importance of findings. There are various types of effect sizes based on the type of statistical analysis being conducted. ## Interpreting Effect Sizes. The proper interpretation of effect sizes will depend on the type of effect measured and the context of the research. Statistical power refers to the probability of detecting a true effect, and it depends on the effect size, sample size, and significance level of a study. One major misinterpretation when it comes to effect sizes is ignoring them and only looking at statistical significance. Effect sizes are crucial for understanding the magnitude and practical importance of statistical findings. Unlike p-values, which only indicate whether an effect is statistically significant, effect sizes provide insight into the strength of a relationship or the difference between groups.
